name: CA-24
label: Safe D

Carbajal holds a massive cash advantage: $3.3 million on hand versus $57,000 for Smith

model.rationale: The district's thirteen-point Democratic lean, Carbajal's incumbency, and his roughly ten-to-one financial advantage over Smith leave little evidence pointing toward an upset, and markets price the race near 98 percent Democratic. With no polls or expert ratings available, the fundamentals-based margin of about 22 points stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Smith consolidating Republican and independent voters, or a surge of outside spending against Carbajal, would be the first sign the margin could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
CA-24 covers California's Central Coast, including Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo, and leans Democratic by about thirteen points. Incumbent Salud Carbajal is seeking another term, and no public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, campaign money, and market pricing.

Carbajal has raised about $1.9 million and holds $3.3 million on hand, while Republican Bob Smith has raised roughly $347,000 with only $57,000 available. Prediction markets put Democratic win odds near 98 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and overwhelming financial advantage points to a comfortable Democratic win, though the lack of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact size of the margin.
